h: Rugby League, Wetlands and a Spot of Art
p: Before you set off, a quick checklist: fill in the waiver online, put everyone in comfy clothes and empty pockets, and make sure the kids have eaten something light. A full belly and a trampoline aren't the best of friends. Grip socks can usually be reused on future visits, so pop them in the car rather than the bin.

During your session, the staff in the park are there to keep things safe, so it's worth reminding excitable little ones to listen to them. One person per trampoline is the golden rule, and it's always better to try tricks you're comfortable with rather than show off for the camera.

Castleford is a proper rugby league town, and the Castleford Tigers are a huge part of local life, so expect a real buzz around the place on match days. The town also sits where the rivers Aire and Calder meet, and the striking Castleford Bridge, a footbridge over the Aire, is a nice spot for a short stroll.

For something calmer after all that bouncing, RSPB Fairburn Ings is close by and has easy trails and hides where you can spot wading birds and waterfowl. Art fans can head to Wakefield for The Hepworth Wakefield, a gallery celebrating Barbara Hepworth, or out to the Yorkshire Sculpture Park near West Bretton, where huge sculptures sit in rolling parkland. Castleford is also the birthplace of sculptor Henry Moore, so it all ties together nicely.
